text:
Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio delivered some good news about Quinyon Mitchell’s status for the Cowboys matchup on Thanksgiving.

“Yeah, I think he’ll be fine,” Fangio said on Tuesday afternoon.

Mitchell suffered a hamstring injury in the second half against the Steelers on Sunday and had to leave early. And he was listed as a non-participant in the Eagles’ first estimated injury report of the week on Monday.

But Fangio thinks Mitchell will be able to play against the Cowboys, which is very good news. Because this is a high-powered Cowboys offense that has put up 91 points over the last two weeks.

“They’ve just got a great offense,” Fangio said. “Their talent level is really, really good at all positions. This is Dak’s, I believe, seventh year in this offense. Because it’s the same offense they ran when Mike McCarthy was there. (Brian) Schottenheimer was an assistant on that staff. He’s kept the offense. I’m sure he’s put a new spin on it here and there.

“When you get a quarterback as good as he is in the same offense for seven straight years or whatever it is, and he’s a really smart player to begin with, your efficiency goes way up.”

The Cowboys have two excellent receivers in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens as their 1-2 punch. Fangio agreed this is the best duo of receivers the Eagles have faced this season.

Lamb in 2026 has 88 catches for 1,108 yards and 9 touchdowns. While Pickens has 57 catches for 780 yards and 6 touchdowns. And even their third receiver, Ryan Flournoy, has 477receiving yards.

While the Eagles hope to have Mitchell, it doesn’t sound like they’ll have Jonathan Jones (ankle), who got some playing time over a healthy Riq Woolen on Sunday before suffering an injury. It looks like it’ll be Mitchell, Woolen and Cooper DeJean against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving.

Woolen after the game admitted he was “annoyed” by being pulled from the game but was able to fight through that to finish off the game. When asked how Woolen has handled all that this week, Fangio said, “Good.”

text:
The New York Giants will reportedly be without one of their top cornerbacks for at least the next month.

Greg Newsome II is set to undergo tightrope surgery on his high ankle sprain and will be sidelined for "roughly" four to six weeks, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Tuesday.

Giants coach John Harbaugh said Monday Newsome had suffered a "serious" high ankle sprain during Sunday's win over the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Harbaugh said at the time Newsome would likely miss "multiple weeks" but that he was unsure as of Monday whether the injury necessitated surgery.

Newsome, who inked a three-year, $46 million extension with the Giants earlier this month, suffered his injury on the opening drive after taking four snaps in Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.

The Athletic's Dan Duggan reported the Giants "taped [Newsome] up and he tried to run on the sideline but was clearly hobbled" before he was ruled out of the game. He was spotted wearing a walking boot in the locker room after the win, per the New York Post's Ryan Dunleavy.

Paulson Adebo, who was a healthy scratch at the back of a cornerback depth chart led by Newsome and Deonte Banks the week prior, stepped up Sunday after Newsome exited against the Jaguars.

Adebo allowed just two catches for 49 yards on eight targets while breaking up two passes and recording an interception, per Pro Football Focus' Bradley Locker.

Harbaugh said after the game Adebo had received a game ball after playing Sunday "like the top-level corner that he is."

Banks also recorded three pass breakups and recorded an interception of his own in the win over the Jaguars.

text:
The New England Patriots desperately need something positive to happen along their offensive line, and head coach Mike Vrabel provided some encouraging information Monday as the team returned from its bye week.

Vrabel indicated that guard Alijah Vera-Tucker could return to practice while fellow offensive lineman Ben Brown might be able to increase his workload. Neither player has been cleared to play against the Los Angeles Chargers, but their potential progress represents a welcome development for an offense that has struggled to establish continuity up front.

With Tommy DeVito preparing to operate the offense in Drake Maye's absence, protecting the quarterback and establishing a dependable rushing attack have become particularly important.

Patriots Have Experienced Significant Offensive Line Turnover

New England placed Vera-Tucker on injured reserve Oct. 22 with a hamstring injury, contributing to a difficult stretch for the interior offensive line. Brown subsequently missed the Patriots' loss to the Detroit Lions with a knee injury.

According to the team's bye-week roster analysis, New England used six different starting offensive line combinations through its first 10 games. That level of turnover makes developing chemistry difficult, particularly when adjacent players must communicate through defensive stunts and blitzes.

The Patriots started Greg Van Roten and Matt Pryor at guard against Detroit. Getting healthier at those positions would give the coaching staff more flexibility when determining its preferred lineup.

MORE: Patriots Reportedly Want to See What Tommy DeVito Can Do Amid Daniel Jones Rumors

Improved Run Blocking Could Help Tommy DeVito

The Patriots have another reason to welcome the potential return of experienced offensive linemen. Their ability to run the football consistently could become increasingly important without Maye.

A productive rushing attack would allow offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels to avoid putting DeVito in predictable passing situations. It could also create opportunities through play-action concepts and help New England sustain drives.

Vera-Tucker's experience and Brown's versatility could prove valuable if both players are healthy enough to contribute. However, their participation in practice throughout the week will provide a better indication of their availability than Monday's initial updates.

New England's offensive problems won't disappear simply because a couple of linemen return. Still, improved depth and continuity would represent meaningful progress for a team that has spent much of the season adjusting to injuries.

Vrabel finally has reason to be encouraged about a position group that will play a significant role in determining how competitive the Patriots remain down the stretch.

title: 49ers urged to consider veteran tackle after Colton McKivitz injury
description:
The loss of right tackle Colton McKivitz was a devastating blow to the San Francisco 49ers' offense.
Once criticized as the weak link on the 49ers' offensive line, McKivitz has developed into a reliable presence over the past two seasons.
While he earned a respectable 72.3 run-blocking grade, his 55.6 pass-blocking grade suggests there is room for improvement.
He believes general manager John Lynch should consider calling 33-year-old veteran offensive tackle Taylor Decker.
The 49ers may hold off on bolstering their offensive line, giving Lowe a chance to establish himself as McKivitz's replacement.
text:
The loss of right tackle Colton McKivitz was a devastating blow to the San Francisco 49ers' offense. Aside from 12-time Pro Bowl left tackle Trent Williams, McKivitz was the team's highest-graded offensive lineman.

Once criticized as the weak link on the 49ers' offensive line, McKivitz has developed into a reliable presence over the past two seasons. He earned a then-career-high 84.2 overall grade from Pro Football Focus in 2025 before surpassing it with an 85.3 grade in 2026.

McKivitz was particularly instrumental in the 49ers' rushing attack, posting a team-best 90.9 run-blocking grade. He also recorded a pass-blocking grade of at least 71.7 in each of his last three seasons and did not allow a sack in 2026.

With McKivitz out for the remainder of the season after suffering a severe leg injury Sunday night against the Minnesota Vikings, the 49ers appear prepared to move forward with Vederian Lowe at right tackle.

Lowe played 38 snaps against the Vikings after replacing McKivitz. While he earned a respectable 72.3 run-blocking grade, his 55.6 pass-blocking grade suggests there is room for improvement. However, across 31 pass-blocking opportunities this season, Lowe hasn't allowed a sack, hit, hurry, or pressure, despite an unremarkable pass-blocking grade of just 30.9.

Michael Moraitis of The Big Lead has a suggestion for the 49ers if the coaching staff isn't entirely confident in Lowe. He believes general manager John Lynch should consider calling 33-year-old veteran offensive tackle Taylor Decker.

The Detroit Lions released Decker in March after the two sides failed to reach an agreement on his salary, with the team reportedly asking the veteran offensive lineman to take a pay cut.

Decker earned an overall grade of at least 74.4 in six of his last seven seasons. The lone exception came in 2025, when he posted a 67.9 grade. Even then, he surrendered just two sacks across 551 pass-blocking snaps.

Moraitis noted that Decker dealt with a chronic right shoulder injury throughout the 2025 season, which could help explain the decline. He could be an option for the 49ers, who strengthened their Super Bowl credentials with Sunday's victory over Minnesota.

"Not long ago, analysts considered Decker one of the better left tackles in the sport. After all, he was a Pro Bowler in 2024 and was a good starter since entering the league in 2016.

"The only potential issue is Decker has just eight career snaps at right tackle. But he should be capable of making that switch if he's willing to, and we have to believe that Decker is capable of playing better in that spot than Lowe is."

The 49ers may hold off on bolstering their offensive line, giving Lowe a chance to establish himself as McKivitz's replacement. San Francisco will get an immediate test of its offensive line depth when it hosts a well-rested Seattle Seahawks team coming off their bye on Sunday at Levi's Stadium.

description:
The Dallas Cowboys returned to the practice field at The Star on Monday afternoon for a brief walkthrough ahead of their Thanksgiving Day showdown against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium.
The Cowboys dropped their first injury report of the week following Monday's session, with starting Pro Bowl tight end Jake Ferguson among the players who did not participate.
But while he did not participate in practice, he is making progress toward a return to the field.
Running back Tyler Goodson, who landed on injured reserve after his breakout game, is battling with ACL and MCL sprains, but also took a positive step forward right alongside Ferguson.
Ferguson, meanwhile, could return as soon as Thanksgiving if he comes along well in practice.
text:
The Dallas Cowboys returned to the practice field at The Star on Monday afternoon for a brief walkthrough ahead of their Thanksgiving Day showdown against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium.

Dallas is fresh off a blowout win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon, but will need to make a quick turnaround. With a quick turnaround come questions about health, and the Cowboys have several players who are continuing to deal with injuries.

The Cowboys dropped their first injury report of the week following Monday's session, with starting Pro Bowl tight end Jake Ferguson among the players who did not participate. But while he did not participate in practice, he is making progress toward a return to the field.

Running back Tyler Goodson, who landed on injured reserve after his breakout game, is battling with ACL and MCL sprains, but also took a positive step forward right alongside Ferguson.

Jake Ferguson, Tyler Goodson Take Positive Step Towards Return

While Goodson and Ferguson did not participate in the practice session, they were on the field and working with the rehab group and Britt Brown, associate athletic trainer and director of rehabilitation and return to play for the Cowboys.

In a photo shared by Tommy Yarrish of the team's official website, Ferguson was working on the cords, which is always a positive sign. Ferguson is recovering from a sprained left PCL and MCL, plus a low ankle sprain.

In Ferguson's absence, Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell have been holding it down for the Cowboys at tight end, while Goodson's absence opened the door for Jashaun Corbin, who impressed the coaching staff with his performance against the Titans on Sunday evening.

And unfortunately for Goodson, he will still be out of action until at least Week 15 against the Los Angeles Rams on December 20. That means Corbin will have more opportunities to impress, while Goodson continues to recover.

Ferguson, meanwhile, could return as soon as Thanksgiving if he comes along well in practice. Or, because of an extended lay-off after Thursday evening's game, the Cowboys could decide to give him one more week to recover before putting him back into the lineup in Week 13 on Monday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks. It will be something to monitor throughout the week.

text:
The NFL enters Week 12 with several notable players dealing with injuries that could affect their availability for upcoming games. With the playoff race beginning to intensify, teams are closely monitoring the health of key offensive players, while some have already received concerning updates regarding their long-term outlook. Here are seven major injury updates to watch heading into Week 12.

MORE: 3 NFL teams that should be worried after Week 11

Brock Bowers continues making progress

Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) continues to make progress, and head coach Klint Kubiak is optimistic about his availability for Week 12. The Raiders will continue monitoring his recovery, but the latest update provides some encouragement regarding his potential return.

Saquon Barkley expects to play in Week 12

Saquon Barkley sustained an injury during Sunday’s victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers, raising questions about his status for the Eagles’ upcoming game. However, when asked whether he believes he will play in Week 12, Barkley responded, “I believe so.” That provides some optimism for Philadelphia heading into its next matchup.

Josh Jacobs was present for Monday’s practice

Josh Jacobs is dealing with a finger injury, but he was present and in uniform for Monday’s practice session. His participation is an encouraging sign as the Packers begin preparations for their Week 12 matchup.

Justin Herbert remains in concussion protocol

Justin Herbert is currently in concussion protocol following his recent injury. His status remains uncertain as the Chargers evaluate his condition and determine whether he will be cleared to return.

MORE: Patrick Mahomes gives very direct, funny answer when asked about his recent success

Bhayshul Tuten avoids a significant setback

Bhayshul Tuten aggravated his ankle injury during Sunday’s loss to the Giants, but the latest testing reportedly indicated that the setback wasn’t too serious. Head coach Liam Coen provided the encouraging update, suggesting the injury may not be as concerning as initially feared.

Terrance Ferguson could require surgery

Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) will not return this season, according to head coach Sean McVay. Ferguson could also require surgery, making this a significant setback as he faces an extended recovery.

Woody Marks trending in the right direction

Woody Marks is recovering from a concussion and appears to be making progress. Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Marks is trending in the right direction and expressed hope that the running back will be available for Week 12, giving Houston some optimism heading into its next game.

The Los Angeles Rams are as banged up as any team in the NFL right now, and have been for most of the season. The defense has gotten relatively healthy, but the offense is missing several key players, including Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson.

The good news is that two players' participation levels in practice improved on Monday. Kyren Williams went from being limited Sunday to being a full participant on Monday, while Kam Curl went from DNP to limited. Sean McVay hasn't expressed any concern about either player missing Wednesday's game against the Packers. There were no other changes on Monday's injury report, aside from four players getting veteran rest days – including Myles Garrett.

title: Antonio Williams avoids serious injury as 'blind' NFL refs ignore banned tackle
description:
The play came early in the fourth quarter of Monday Night Football with the Bengals leading the Commanders 17-13.
Hill grabbed the receiver and pulled him backward while dropping his weight, causing Williams' legs to get caught beneath the defender.
The Washington wideout fell awkwardly but got back to his feet and apparently avoided serious injury or a hip-drop tackle flag.
A confirmed hip-drop tackle typically carries a 15-yard penalty and an automatic first down.
Hill was fined $14,731 for unnecessary roughness during a game against the Seattle Seahawks for his only recorded career NFL fine.
text:
Antonio Williams escaped what appeared to be a blatant hip-drop tackle scare before the Washington Commanders defeated the Cincinnati Bengals, but not before the internet voiced their outrage online

Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams escaped a tackle that had the team's fans fearing the worst, but NFL officials kept their flags tucked away, and Cincinnati Bengals cornerback Daxton Hill avoided a penalty for a collision that resembled the league's banned hip-drop technique.

The play came early in the fourth quarter of Monday Night Football with the Bengals leading the Commanders 17-13. Jayden Daniels threw a pass over the middle to Williams, who caught the ball and turned upfield before Hill brought him down from behind.

Hill grabbed the receiver and pulled him backward while dropping his weight, causing Williams' legs to get caught beneath the defender. The Washington wideout fell awkwardly but got back to his feet and apparently avoided serious injury or a hip-drop tackle flag.

NFL fans were shocked to see no flag thrown on the field even though Hill got up and returned to the action. Viewers questioned why officials allowed a move that fit the league's criteria for the technique that the NFL outlawed in 2024.

"Textbook definition of a hip drop tackle," one fan wrote. Another complained, "Good old NFL officiating right there," as frustration spread over the lack of a call.

The NFL's 2026 rulebook prohibits a defender from grabbing or wrapping a runner, then unweighting himself by swiveling and dropping his hips or lower body onto, or trapping, the runner's legs at or below the knee.

All of those elements are required for a violation, and each box appeared to be checked during replays of he play. A confirmed hip-drop tackle typically carries a 15-yard penalty and an automatic first down.

While officials can miss a foul during live action, the NFL can still review video afterward and impose discipline regardless of whether a penalty was called.

Last season, the NFL admitted it had incorrectly taken away Isaiah Likely's touchdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers, which could have affected the AFC North playoff picture.

Under an updated NFL-NFLPA framework, a player who accumulates three violations in the same emphasized safety category can face an automatic one-game suspension, with hip-drop tackles among the five categories covered.

There was no immediate indication that Hill would be fined or found responsible for a violation. Hill was fined $14,731 for unnecessary roughness during a game against the Seattle Seahawks for his only recorded career NFL fine.

Williams led all receivers with 122 yards on nine catches as the Commanders improved to 4-5-1 and jumped out of last place in the NFC East.

text:
RENTON, Wash. -- The Seattle Seahawks still plan to start Sam Darnold against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday but will wait to see how the quarterback looks in practice Wednesday before making a final decision, coach Mike Macdonald said.

Darnold has missed the past two games because of a quad injury he suffered near the end of Seattle's loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8, when he also suffered a cracked rib on his first dropback of the night. Macdonald said last Monday that Darnold would start this week as long as he made the progress over the bye that the team was projecting.

Speaking with reporters Monday, Macdonald said the quarterback made "a good bit of progress."

"He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here," Macdonald said. "He also was able to get away. He's optimistic, but I think just with today's practice cadence and speed today, I think it's probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday's practice."

The Seahawks held a bonus practice Monday coming off their bye. They were not required to release an injury report, but Darnold -- who had not practiced since the Nov. 2 Bears game -- was seen jogging out for warmups with his helmet on, and Macdonald confirmed that he took part.

"He looked great," the coach said. "Everything was positive today. He took a ton of reps, but it wasn't a full-speed -- it was more of a [walk-through] tempo."

With the first-place 49ers (9-1) winning Sunday night, the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks (6-4) are now three games back in the NFC West standings heading into Sunday's game at Levi's Stadium. San Francisco won the first meeting at Lumen Field in October.

Darnold's quad and rib injuries were the latest setbacks in what has been a trying start to the season. He injured his glute on the fifth play of the opener, missing the remainder of that game and the following week. In six full games, he has thrown 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions.

Backup Drew Lock, meanwhile, has thrown seven touchdown passes with zero interceptions over the four games in which he has filled in -- all Seattle victories. Lock has been dealing with a right elbow injury for over a month, and he also played through an oblique injury last week while quarterbacking Seattle to a win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

"I'd say the bye week was really helpful for Drew," Macdonald said. "I think a well-deserved chance for him to feel better, and that's going to help us moving forward. But I think that's the case for several of our guys as well."

Macdonald did not have injury updates on any other players Monday. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams missed the past two games with a stinger that kept him out of practice both weeks. He was on the field for warmups Monday with his helmet.

Players not seen during the warmup period Monday included right tackle Abe Lucas, right guard Anthony Bradford and left guard Quenton Nelson. Lucas left the Raiders game and did not return after suffering an ankle sprain. Nelson, acquired in an Oct. 27 trade with the Indianapolis Colts, is recovering from a knee procedure that kept him out of the past two games. Bradford has started in Nelson's absence, but he has been dealing with a knee injury.

text:
Puka Nacua’s season with the Los Angeles Rams is over. Nacua underwent knee surgery last week, and the procedure formally knocks him out for the rest of the season. The Rams now face the stretch run without one of the most prolific weapons in the NFL.

The surgery is, somehow, only part of the big Nacua news to come out of the end of last week. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler appeared on a segment on ESPN and was asked what the injury means for Nacua’s future with the Rams. Fowler’s assessment was blunt.

ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler states that Puka Nacua’s injury ‘probably’ ends his tenure with the Los Angeles Rams

“Going into free agency, (Nacua) has got two significant injuries, including a significant MCL injury that Sean McVay, the head coach, says will keep him out a few months. Probably ends his tenure with the Rams. Plus the three-game suspension for the off-field stuff this offseason. So it’s just not the kind of way you want to go into free agency with momentum.”

— ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler on Los Angeles Rams WR Puka Nacua

“Probably ends his tenure with the Rams.” Oh! The use of ‘probably’ here is…something. It is at a minimum interesting.

A healthy Nacua is one of the NFL’s best players. He is a focal point of the Los Angeles offense, and his production has made him one of the most dangerous pass catchers in football. Players like that don’t typically become available on the open market. Especially at 25 years of age. Nacua turns 26 next May. That is, presumably, right in the heart of his prime. Players like this usually get paid and stay put.

Fowler’s comments suggest a different outcome is very much on the table. And that could be influenced by the things Fowler laid out about the last 12 months for Nacua. After all, these wide receiver contracts have exploded over the last two years — and Nacua has two 1,500+ yards from scrimmage seasons in four years. The production is elite.

The question isn’t whether Nacua is good enough between the lines to deserve a long-term commitment. Of course he is. The question is what kind of price the Rams, or any team for that matter, are willing to pay to keep him when there are legitimate questions about plenty of non-football variables. Fowler seems to think it may lead to a split in the months ahead.

text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Welcome back, Micah Parsons.

The Green Bay Packers' star pass rusher was cleared Monday to return from last season's knee injury and is expected to make his 2026 debut Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Rams, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Earlier Monday, Parsons said he still needed final clearance from Dr. Neal ElAttrache, who performed the surgery.

Parsons, who injured his left knee in Week 15 last season, still needs to be officially activated off the physically unable to perform list. That move did not happen before the end of NFL business Monday.

Parsons' return to game action will come 347 days after he not only tore his ACL but also his meniscus in a noncontact injury against the Denver Broncos.

Parsons first returned to practice Nov. 4 and did only individual drills that week. The following week, he began to incorporate team (11-on-11) drills into his work. The Packers then had their bye following the Nov. 15 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, but it was not a full bye week because of the Thanksgiving Eve game. The Packers resumed practice Saturday and practiced for three days before they depart for Los Angeles on Tuesday.

"I would say I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday but for sure this season," Parsons said Monday. "And I'll be looking forward to returning to the field."

Parsons is expected to be on a snap count upon his return.

Despite having a winning record (6-4), the Packers sit in last place in the NFC North, where the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions and Vikings are all 7-2.

"I'm so locked in on what's ahead of me and I understand what this game Wednesday means to the organization and I myself and what it means for playoffs," Parsons said. "And if I can be out there, I want to be out there and I'm excited for any time. Because we only got seven more games left, so I want to capitalize on all those if I can."

Parsons led the Packers with 12.5 sacks last season and led the entire league with 64 pressures, according to ESPN Analytics, despite playing in only 14 games. It was his first season in Green Bay after the Packers gave up two first-round picks plus defensive tackle Kenny Clark to acquire Parsons from the Dallas Cowboys just days before the start of last season.

But the Packers did not win a game after Parsons was injured last season. They were 9-3-1 heading into the Broncos game but lost five in a row, including an NFC wild-card playoff game against the Bears, to close the season. Without Parsons, the Packers have gone 6-9.

"The only thing I'm targeting in a sense of mindset is to win every week to try to uplift this season, change this season around and do exactly what the Packers brought me here to do," Parsons said. "That's it. That's my only target and that's to make a run for the playoffs and make guys around me better. That's it."

"So I have no targets and outcomes," Parsons added. "I think I've achieved everything that I've wanted in my career except for the big one and I think that's kind of like my own mindset and through the [Nick] Saban documentary I learned just stay in the process of every day. Own my process my today, so I owned it today. I got another process tomorrow and, God willing, I'll have another process Wednesday night and that'll be the start of this new journey."

INDIANAPOLIS — The budding partnership between Seth McGowan and Jonathan Taylor has to be put on hold for a while.

McGowan, the Colts rookie running back who has emerged as arguably the offense’s second-best playmaker in a lost season, suffered a hamstring injury in last week’s 26-3 loss in Houston.

Indianapolis has now had four days to evaluate the injury, and it appears that McGowan’s hamstring injury is serious enough to keep him out for a while.

“He's going to miss some time,” Indianapolis head coach Shane Steichen said Monday. “I'm not going to put a timetable on it, but he'll miss some time.”

When Steichen uses the phrase “miss some time,” the Colts coach typically means a player will miss multiple weeks.

It is unclear if McGowan will be placed on injured reserve. If McGowan is placed on injured reserve, he would have to miss a minimum of four weeks.

The Colts have six games remaining in the season.

With McGowan out, Indianapolis signed former Giants and Browns running back Eric Gray to the practice squad on Monday. D.J. Giddens, the second-year back McGowan beat out for the backup job behind Taylor, slides into the No. 2 role.

Giddens has seven carries for 48 yards this season. The 2025 fifth-rounder has never gotten a whole lot of chances behind Taylor.

“Yeah, it creates opportunity for Giddens for sure, and obviously we’ve got (undrafted rookie Davon) Booth on the roster, a practice squad guy,” Steichen said.

None of those players are likely to carry as much responsibility as McGowan.

For years, the Colts had been reluctant to take carries away from Taylor, who leads Indianapolis with 760 yards and eight touchdowns in 2026. Even when Indianapolis had Zack Moss on the roster, a capable back who filled in nicely for an injured Taylor, Steichen’s staff gave almost all of the carries to Taylor.

McGowan broke through that barrier.

The seventh-round rookie out of Kentucky had 292 yards on 58 carries this season, and his role was increasing before the injury. McGowan averaged 8.5 carries for 49.3 yards in the four games before his injury, topping out at 12 carries for 77 yards in a win over the Dolphins.

“That's just kind of evolved as the season has went on,” Steichen said. “He’s just a hard runner, good change of pace. … The physicality that he runs with, the way he’s seeing it right now, running through arm tackles, it's been pretty impressive to see.”

McGowan has also been an electric return man, ranked third in the NFL at 29.2 yards per kickoff return this season.

Indianapolis has Ashton Dulin and Anthony Gould to step in for McGowan in the return game.

Replacing the rookie at running back will be much more difficult.

Detroit Lions cornerback D.J. Reed took a positive step in his return from a hip injury Monday, Nov. 23, and could play in this week's Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears.

Reed said he ran at full speed before Monday's walk-through and felt "like my explosiveness came back and my twitchiness." The Lions listed Reed as a full participant on their estimated practice report.

“If I am out there that means that I’m ready and I’m confident to go," he said. "So that’s going to be determined on Thursday, but like I said today was a pretty good step for me."

title: 5 Takeaways: Chargers HC Jim Harbaugh Provides Injury Update on Justin Herbert
description:

text:
The Chargers are 1-9 ahead of a Week 12 home game with the New England Patriots.

Here are five takeaways from Chargers Head Coach Jim Harbaugh's Monday press conference:

1. Herbert 'in concussion protocol'

Chargers Head Coach Jim Harbaugh provided an update on quarterback Justin Herbert on Monday.

Harbaugh said the Chargers quarterback entered the league's concussion protocol following Sunday’s game against the Jets.

"After the game, reported symptoms to the trainers and the doctors," Harbaugh said.

He later added: "Justin will be in the concussion protocol."

Per the league's concussion protocol, he will need to progress through all the steps of the protocol before being cleared to play.

With a lot left to be determined as the week goes on, the Chargers currently have one other quarterback on the active roster in DJ Uiagalelei, with veteran Jake Browning on the practice squad.

Uiagalelei recently made his NFL debut in the fourth quarter of Week 9, throwing for 24 yards and a touchdown pass.

"[Uiagalelei] would be the next man up, and then we would bring Jake Browning up as well," Harbaugh said.

The Chargers next game is at home once again in a Week 12 matchup against the Patriots at SoFi Stadium.

2. Other injury updates

Harbaugh also provided updates on other injuries around the roster.

Running back Keaton Mitchell left the game in the first quarter and was labeled as questionable to return with a knee injury during Sunday's game against the Jets.

He would later return to the game in the middle of the second quarter and returned a kickoff as he finished the afternoon playing four total snaps on both offense and special teams.

"We'll see how he responds to treatment this week," Harbaugh said of Mitchell.

Chargers first-round Akheem Mesidor also left the game in the second quarter with an ankle injury and played 12 defensive snaps.

"Akheem, ankle, [we'll] see how he responds this week to treatment," Harbaugh said.

Similar could be said about a pair of Chargers who were inactive in Week 11.

Daiyan Henley did not practice during the week with a knee injury and was ruled out, while Tarheeb Still was added to the injury report on Friday and missed Sunday's game.

"They'll keep attacking the rehab and we'll see where the week takes us with Daiyan and Tarheeb Still," Harbaugh said.

He later added: "I think with both, treatment and see how the week goes."

3. Run game continues to build

Sunday marked back-to-back weeks with a good Chargers performance on the ground.

The Bolts ran the ball a total of 30 times for 158 yards against New York, averaging 5.3 yards per carry.

They almost equaled their season-high mark from last week and have now tallied a total of 318 rushing yards over the last two weeks, the most in the NFL.

It has coincided with an improvement Harbaugh has seen from the unit overall, as they're also eighth in the NFL in EPA per play (0.106) in that timeframe.

"I think it was, by my judgement, some real improvements on the offensive side of the ball," Harbaugh said. "Efficiency was big when it came to the ground game… it was an efficient offense."

A big part of it has been the play of Omarion Hampton, who continues ascending as the team's leader on the ground.

The second year running back added another 89 yards on 14 attempts (6.4 yards a rush), including an explosive 36-yard run to open the fourth quarter, his longest of the year.

Hampton now has 194 rushing yards and a touchdown over the last pair of games, the fifth-most in the NFL.

"I think with the touches, rhythm, the confidence," Harbaugh said about Hampton. "He's seeing things really well. He's an ascending player all the way.

"Good yards after contact, he's really seeing things well, good shoulder lean," he added. "Running very well."

Hampton's ability to break tackles has been a key, with 151 of his rushing yards coming after contact, good for fourth-most in the NFL.

He's now up to 138 carries for 563 yards and four rushing scores, and has been on an upward trajectory with his workload increasing over the past couple of weeks.

"I think it's worked well and been a positive," Harbaugh said.

He later added: "He's certainly responded like the really good player that he is."

4. A look at the defense

After getting a chance to watch the tape back from Sunday, Harbaugh recapped the defensive performance.

The Chargers defense allowed the Jets offense to be efficient throughout the afternoon, averaging 5.8 yards per play, not forcing a turnover and not forcing a punt.

The main factor to Harbaugh came in bringing down the Jets offensive players — something that allowed them to extend drives and hold onto the ball.

"A lot of yards after contact, things we're addressing," Harbaugh said. "Tackling, angles, some technique things. Things we were really great at the week before."

The group allowed 37 carries for 165 rushing yards on the ground, good for 4.5 yards a carry.

And according to PFF, they allowed 115 of those yards after contact to go along with 93 yards after the catch.

"We were giving up a lot of yardage on first down, second-and 10 and the Jets were converting on third down," Harbaugh said. "You tip your hat off to them, they did it at a high level, turnover free.

"Five possessions in a row scoring, they didn't turn the ball over," Harbaugh added. "It was a well-played game."

These extra yards ended up getting the Jets in more favorable positions, finishing the day allowing nine of 11 third down conversions, with six of the attempts coming on third-and 3 or closer.

"The yards after contact, the runs that bled yardage," Harbaugh said. "It wasn't the stop them, knockback type of tackle. Some of it had to do with the angle, some of it had to do with the technique.

"I think that was the biggest difference," he added.

5. Awosika gets start at RG

The Chargers starting offensive line went through a change in Week 11.

Veteran Kayode Awosika got the nod at right guard against the Jets, playing all 60 snaps in the afternoon.

It was his second game being active since returning from a fibula injury he suffered in Week 2, as he played only on special teams against Baltimore.

Cole Strange had started every game at right guard before this past week.

"Really based on the practices 'Yode has had the last couple of weeks," Harbaugh said. "He was a starter when he got hurt, worked his way back.

"I thought he acquitted himself well in the game," Harbaugh added.

According to PFF, Awosika allowed just one pressure against New York and finished with the team's second-highest pass blocking grade (82.0) behind Joe Alt.

When asked if starting Awosika was a move just for the week, or moving forward, Harbaugh said it will come down to how things shake out in practice.

"We'll base it on practice, but I think he played well enough to start again," Harbaugh said.

Eagles cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant to kick off a short week of prep before the Eagles play the Cowboys on Thanksgiving in Dallas.

The Eagles didn’t actually practice on Monday, so their injury report was an estimation.

Not only was Mitchell (hamstring) listed as a non-participant, but so was fellow cornerback Jonathan Jones (ankle). Both players got hurt in the win over the Steelers on Sunday. Mitchell was seen getting on a stationary bike in the post-game locker room, while Jones was in a walking boot on his right foot.

If neither are available, the Eagles would potentially start Riq Woolen and Kelee Ringo against a high-powered Cowboys offense in Dallas. Although, the Eagles could also move Cooper DeJean to outside corner and replace him with either Michael Carter or Kenny Moore.

Mitchell was playing very well on Sunday against DK Metcalf before Metcalf was tossed and Mitchell left with his injury. Woolen was actually benched in the second quarter but had to re-enter the game after injuries.

Here’s the Eagles’ first injury report of the week:

DNP: CB Jonathan Jones (ankle), CB Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring), OLB Arnold Ebiketie (oblique), LB Smael Mondon (ankle)

NFL

Limited: RB Saquon Barkley (neck/illness), TE Dallas Goedert (shin), QB Tanner McKee (rib), RB Will Shipley (foot/illness)

Full: DT Jalen Carter (quad), DB Michael Carter (abdomen), WR Britain Covey (knee), OLB Jonathan Greenard (ankle), WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring)

It’s good news that Barkley was listed as a limited participant to start the week after leaving the Steelers game early with what appeared to be a stinger. Barkley came off the field holding his left arm limp at one point. He had a stinger earlier in the season too.

We’ll also monitor Dallas Goedert’s injury the rest of this week, but the fact that he was limited on Monday seems like a good sign for his availability on Thursday.

text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Micah Parsons stopped short Monday of declaring himself good to go, but the Packers' All-Pro edge rusher said he believes he’s done “everything I possibly could” to return.

After Dec. 29 surgery to repair a torn ACL and torn meniscus in his left knee, Parsons has been medically cleared and is set to make his season debut on Wednesday against the Los Angeles Rams, according to multiple reports.

Parsons said he is eager to play in his first game since he was injured in a Dec. 14 loss at Denver. The Packers didn't win another game the rest of last season, finishing on a five-game skid that included an NFC wild card playoff meltdown against the Chicago Bears.

With his team at 6-4 and fighting for an NFC playoff spot entering the final seven games of the season, Parsons knows how critical the game is.

Parsons still needs to be activated from the physically unable to perform list by Wednesday in order to play against the host Rams (6-4).

“I understand what this game Wednesday means to the organization and (to) myself — and what it means for playoffs,” Parsons said. “And if I can be out there, I want to be out there. We’ve only got seven more games left, so I want to capitalize on all those if I can.”

The Packers are tied for seventh in the NFL in sacks (29) and rank second in the league in takeaways (20). Parsons had 12 1/2 sacks last season for the Packers after they acquired him from the Dallas Cowboys at the end of training camp.

“I think it’s only going to make us better,” safety Javon Bullard said of Parsons' return. “With (No.) 1 on the field, we’re a better team. We’re a better defense. He’s going to up everybody else’s game, and we’re going to up his game. I think that’s what makes this defense special.”

It's hard to say how much Parsons would play against the Rams. Last year, when he made his Packers debut in a season-opening win over Detroit, Parsons played 30 of 67 snaps (45%) after doing very little in training camp and joining the roster just nine days before that game.

“I think once I’m in the zone, I’m in the zone and people don’t really mess with you when you’re in a zone,” Parsons replied when asked if he would adhere to limits on his snaps. “I think where we’re at in the season — like I said, every win matters.

text:
LOS ANGELES -- Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson's ankle injury will require season-ending surgery, head coach Sean McVay said Monday.

Ferguson has been on injured reserve since spraining his ankle in Week 3. The Rams opened his 21-day practice window on Nov. 4 with the intent of him playing against the Washington Commanders that Sunday.

But Ferguson injured his hamstring in practice that Friday, putting him out a couple more weeks. On Nov. 11, McVay said the team's goal was to have a roster spot open for the tight end by the time the practice window closed, even if he wasn't ready to play.

But on Monday, McVay said Ferguson's ankle is "just not responding the way that you want." The tight end will not be added to the active roster before the end of his 21-day practice window, which will end his season.

McVay was asked whether Ferguson had a setback with his ankle injury.

"I think it was more along the lines of pushing to get back, didn't necessarily feel great, but he had a really good week of practice," McVay said. "But you could still see it was kind of getting comfortable, took some meds to be able to do that, gets the hamstring on the Friday.

"And then as he's really been attacking both of these injuries, you get another look at it and it was like something in his deltoid in his ankle that really is just not healing the way that you want, unfortunately. And so as a result of that, I don't know if it was necessarily a specific setback as much as it's just not coming along and he wouldn't be able to be himself."

Ferguson was a second-round pick in the 2025 draft. In 17 career games, he has 18 catches for 294 yards and four touchdowns.

The situation around Terrance Ferguson's injury has taken another devastating turn, with the Los Angeles Rams tight end now set to undergo season-ending ankle surgery.

The 23-year-old originally injured his left ankle during the Rams' loss to the Broncos on September 27, suffering a medial ankle sprain that forced him to leave the game. He briefly returned before aggravating the injury and was ultimately placed on injured reserve on October 2.

“I don’t know if it was necessarily a specific setback as much as it’s just not coming along,” head coach Sean McVay said. “He wouldn’t be able to put his foot in the ground, and a lot of the things that his game is predicated on is being that twitchy athlete.”

Read More on NFL

Ferguson started working his way back in November, opening his 21-day practice window before the Rams' Week 9 matchup against the Commanders. The expectation was that he could return after the team's Week 11 bye, but unfortunately the ankle hasn't improved, and now the second-year tight end will need surgery.

It's another brutal setback for LA's offense, which has already lost Puka Nacua to a season-ending knee injury, and with Davante Adams still on IR.

More news: Colts Provide Major Update on Star WR Alec Pierce After Lengthy Injury Absence

Ferguson entered the 2026 season with massive hype. The Rams selected him 46th overall in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Oregon, and he made several explosive plays during his rookie season, finishing the year with 231 yards and three touchdowns on just 11 catches, averaging a whopping 21 yards per catch, the highest mark among tight ends.

With the Rams running the most 13 personnel (three tight ends) of any team in the league, Ferguson was a popular breakout pick this season and expected to give Matthew Stafford a third reliable option next to Nacua and Adams. Unfortunately, his season has ended after just three games, finishing with just seven catches for 63 yards and one touchdown.

With the injuries to Nacua and Adams, the Rams were counting on Ferguson to come back and be a consistent contributor down the stretch. But with him now gone, they'll have to lean even more on tight ends Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, and Davis Allen, along with a wide receiver trio of Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, and Tutu Atwell.

LA is still in the playoff hunt at 6-4, but has a brutal upcoming stretch with games against the Packers, Chiefs, 49ers, Cowboys, Buccaneers, and Seahawks (twice).

text:
The Houston Texans saw one of their players start Thursday night's game against the Indianapolis Colts about as badly as you could imagine.

On the opening kickoff against the Colts, Texans defensive end Chris Braswell–– called up in his first game of the season from the practice squad–– suffered a serious leg injury trying to defend an Indianapolis return.

The injury led to Braswell being carted off while his leg was placed in an air cast, and made up for quite literally the worst outcome you could expect from a player making their season debut from the practice squad.

And now, as the Texans have returned from their mini-bye, Houston has officially placed Braswell on the practice squad injured reserve, unofficially ending his season.

Texans' Unofficially End Chris Braswell's Season With IR Designation

It's no surprise that Braswell's going to miss an extended amount of time with the serious knee injury he suffered last weekend, and the newest injured reserve designation from the team only confirms that even further.

We still don't have clarity on exactly what the diagnosis is for Braswell's injury. But an injured reserve designation tells us that it's significant enough to take him off the practice squad for the remainder of the season.

Technically, the Texans' injured reserve designation––even while being on the practice squad––will leave Braswell out of the mix for a minimum of four games, thus leaving room for him to return before the end of the season.

But even if Braswell's injury was somehow not as serious as it initially appeared on Thursday night, the team has just one more activation to utilize over the next seven weeks due to the previous injured reserve activations that Houston has used this year.

Therefore, that means Houston will have to be extra careful about where they decide to spend that injured reserve activation over the next few weeks, if they want said player to return before the end of the regular season.

Any player on the practice squad injured reserve, such as Braswell, or even running back Jawhar Jordan, doesn't usually have the greatest chance of getting that activation to swing their way.

For Braswell, it's the end of his third season in the league since being a second-round selection to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the 2024 NFL Draft, and his first season as a member of the Texans.

Braswell, in his first two seasons with the Buccaneers, had appeared in 35 games to record 48 tackles, five tackles for loss, a forced fumble, and 2.5 sacks.

The Texans have had Braswell off and on the practice squad since he was waived from Tampa Bay in August earlier this year, and he was elevated for his first appearance on the gameday roster last Wednesday.

Overall, Braswell projected as an intriguing upside swing for the Texans to have onboard the roster who finally got his opportunity in Week 11, but now will have to wait until 2027 to get back onto the field.

title: Cowboys Injury Update: Schottenheimer Provides Latest on 2 Defensive Starters
description:
The Dallas Cowboys improved to 5-6 on the season with a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 11.
First, it was linebacker Dee Winters who had to be helped off the field following an apparent knee injury.
Neither player returned to action against the Titans, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Durant could have.
After the game, Schottenheimer spoke with reporters and said that Winters had a knee contusion, but didn't elaborate on his status.
Schottenheimer added that the Cowboys decided to play it safe with the game in hand, keeping Durant on the bench.
text:
The Dallas Cowboys improved to 5-6 on the season with a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 11. The Cowboys had a lot go their way on offense, but once again, their defense left a lot to be desired.

They also saw two of their key starters go down with injuries. First, it was linebacker Dee Winters who had to be helped off the field following an apparent knee injury. After that, they lost Cobie Durant who took a hard hit to the head.

Neither player returned to action against the Titans, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Durant could have.

After the game, Schottenheimer spoke with reporters and said that Winters had a knee contusion, but didn't elaborate on his status. As for Durant, he said he was evaluated for a concussion but was cleared to play. Schottenheimer added that the Cowboys decided to play it safe with the game in hand, keeping Durant on the bench.

Durant is already filling in for an injured DaRon Bland, which would leave Dallas very thin at the position should Durant miss any time. With him out, the Cowboys turned to Ameer Speed, who has been a pleasant surprise this year.

Interestingly enough, the Cowboys turned to Justin Barron when Winters went down, rather than DeMarvion Overshown. Eventually, Overshown was on the field, but it appears he's fallen out of favor with the coaching staff ever since he was penalized for running onto the field in street clothes to celebrate during the win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Dallas has a short week as they will host the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 12 on Thanksgiving Day. They only have a few days to rest up before taking the field again, so these injuries need to be monitored.

Dak Prescott also dealing with an injury, but doesn't seem concerned

Another injury popped up after the game as Dak Prescott was seen with his left hand in a wrap. Thankfully, it's not his throwing hand, so that's a plus. Also, Prescott didn't seem to be worried about it at all.

Prescott said that "it bent back on a bad hit he took in the second half." He added that it was a "blessing" that the injury wasn't more serious. Prescott has had injury concerns in the past, but has been able to play in every game over the past two seasons.

text:
The San Francisco 49ers lost their starting right tackle Colton McKivitz to a gruesome injury during their Week 11 "Sunday Night Football" game against the Minnesota Vikings.

McKivitz was injured after blocking on a Christian McCaffrey run in the latter half of the second quarter. The 30-year-old tackle was rolled up in a pile as McCaffrey was tackled and as McKivitz came out of the pile, his left foot was facing the wrong direction.

McKivitz's 49ers teammates were immediately upset looking at the tackle's injury. Christian McCaffrey fell to a knee looking at him while Trent Williams was shown on the broadcast looking dismayed, and he forcibly spiked his helmet into the ground.

McKivitz was quickly tended to by medical staff on the field and was carted into the locker room as a result of his injury. Swing tackle Vederian Lowe checked into the game to replace him.

Colton McKivitz injury update

49ers coach Kyle Shanahan provided an update about McKivitz's status after the game. He told reporters McKivitz suffered a fractured and dislocated left ankle and will miss the remainder of the season because of it, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner.

McKivitz entered play Sunday having played all 563 snaps for the 49ers offense, one of two San Francisco linemen to do that along with left guard Connor Colby.

What happened to Colton McKivitz?

McKivitz was injured while blocking on a Christian McCaffrey run. McCaffrey was tackled on the play and the veteran running back landed directly on the back of McKivitz's left leg.

McKivitz remained down on the field after the play and eventually rolled out of the pile, revealing that his left foot was facing the wrong way.

Who is Colton McKivitz's backup?

Vederian Lowe is McKivitz's backup. The five-year veteran was originally selected by the Vikings in the fifth round of the 2022 NFL Draft and has appeared in 55 career games with 25 starts, all of which came with the New England Patriots.

Lowe spent the previous three seasons with the Patriots and was a part of the team that made it to Super Bowl 60. Now, he will be tasked with starting in place of McKivitz with the 30-year-old right tackle set to miss the rest of the season.

49ers OT depth chart

The 49ers have four offensive tackles on their 53-man roster. Below is a look at the pecking order within the unit.

Trent Williams (left tackle)

Colton McKivitz (right tackle)

Vederian Lowe

Enrique Cruz Jr.

Cruz, a fifth-round rookie out of Kansas, is inactive for Sunday's game but will likely be active in future games as the team's swing tackle with McKivitz sidelined.

The 49ers also have Foster Sarell, who has appeared in 41 games (four starts) with the Los Angeles Chargers, and Isaac Alarcon of the International Player Pathway available on their practice squad to help man the position.

Additionally, San Francisco has Austen Pleasants, who appeared in 15 games for them last season with one start, on IR with a return designation. It isn't clear when he will be ready to return, but he could also be an option to replenish the team's tackle depth.

This story will be updated as more information becomes available.

authors: Jordan Raanan, Katherine Terrell, NFL Nation, Dan Graziano, ESPN staff, Michael Dirocco, Eric Karabell, ESPN Fantasy, Todd Archer, Eric Woodyard
description:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Cam Skattebo's pledge to nix his trademark backflip didn't last long.
Skattebo flexed and let out a primal scream after running for a first down with two minutes remaining in the contest.
Quarterback J.J. McCarthy kneeled on the ball three times after the backflip to close out the game.

text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Cam Skattebo's pledge to nix his trademark backflip didn't last long. Not even a week. "Second nature" took over, the New York Giants running back said.

Several days after declaring he would put the backflip on the shelf after watching Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson get injured celebrating a sack, Skattebo went back to the well. He couldn't resist after icing a 23-18 win for the Giants over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.

"He couldn't help himself, could he?" coach John Harbaugh said with a smirk. "Just couldn't help himself."

Skattebo flexed and let out a primal scream after running for a first down with two minutes remaining in the contest. He then turned and flipped in the middle of the field with the game all but over. Harbaugh seemed to mouth "Wow" after seeing the flip.

Jacksonville couldn't stop the clock when play resumed with no timeouts remaining.

"I kind of thought about it. I wanted to give one last one to my fans," Skattebo said. "At the end of the day, when the energy calls for it and I have to bring the juice for the team. When I backflip it brings juice to these guys. It shows how much I care. I play with my heart and soul in this game. ... When it's called for, it's second nature. It's hard to hold back from."

It's the second straight game in which Skattebo did a backflip. He also did it (along with wide receivers Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields) after a touchdown in last Thursday's loss to the Washington Commanders.

Skattebo, who returned from a serious ankle injury suffered last year, didn't exactly say earlier in the week that he would retire the backflip forever. He conceded on Wednesday that the backflip might resurface "if we go to the playoffs or something."

He didn't seem to think the following Sunday would be the time. But it was. The emotion of it all took over.

"Obviously I don't want to do them because of the injury that happened, but it brings energy to this team," he said. "If I have to do it because the energy is low and we have a good moment, then that is what's going to happen."

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy kneeled on the ball three times after the backflip to close out the game. Skattebo rushed three times for 13 yards on that final drive and finished with 34 yards on 14 carries.

The backflip was a point of contention throughout the offseason, even before Hutchinson had his mishap. Skattebo did his flip for the first time since his ankle injury after hitting a home run at the Brian Burns Celebrity Softball Game in late May.

Skattebo then stumbled while doing a backflip at Fanatics Fest over the summer, creating a stir.

Giants brass had a conversation with Skattebo afterward. It preferred he didn't do it leading into the season, especially coming off a major injury, but didn't mandate he never do it again.

Harbaugh seemed happy this past week that Skattebo seemed to come to the conclusion he did on his own.

"I think it's good. I'm happy for it," Harbaugh said. "I support his decision, and I hope he scores a lot of touchdowns. I hope he gets an opportunity to prove it real soon. That'd be great."

It wasn't a touchdown, but the opportunity presented itself for Skattebo on Sunday when he helped secure a win. And he took it, without hesitation.

text:
San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome leg injury that will likely keep him out for the rest of the season after he was carted off the field against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.

"It's brutal," 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey said, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner. "He's somebody that is one of the heart and souls of this team, a guy who shows up every day with the right attitude. He's the standard, and we're going to really miss him. We all love him. We're praying for him. It's one of the worst parts about this game is stuff like that, but we love him and we're going to play for him from here on out."

Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes sent his well wishes upon seeing the injury.

The injury comes amid what has been a career year for McKivitz, who has the second-best PFF run block grade among tackles and the seventh-best overall grade among tackles.

McKivitz has been a starter on the Niners' offensive line and has played all 17 games of the season since 2023. He has yet to miss a game this season, though that streak will surely come to an end.

While McKivitz has established himself as a starter, the 30-year-old has had a long road to get to that point. He was a fifth-round draft pick in 2020 and started a handful of games as a rookie, but was waived ahead of the 2021 season, and had to work his way back onto the active roster via the practice squad.

Eventually, he earned the job as a full-time starter ahead of the 2023 campaign, and he's stayed there ever since. He signed a three-year, $45 million deal this offseason despite perhaps being able to earn more elsewhere.

"I want to be on that 10-year wall," McKivitz said after signing that deal. "I don't want to leave here. Obviously being cut, I've got some scars there. But, there was a reason why I was drafted here, why I was cut here, and why I still play here. Now I've had three good seasons of starting and I'm going into the fourth."

But the franchise quarterback took six more sacks to bring his season total to 39, a league high.

Herbert previously suffered an injury to the middle finger of his left (non- throwing) hand earlier this month, but it wasn’t fractured and he was able to play through it.

If Herbert does not clear the protocol in time for the Chargers’ Week 12 home game against the New England Patriots on Nov. 29, DJ Uiagalelei would be in line to start under center. Los Angeles is 1-9, tied with ‌Tennessee and ​Miami for the worst record in the league.

–The Jacksonville Jaguars left their 23-18 loss to the New York Giants with injury ​concerns for left tackle Walker Little, running back Bhayshul Tuten and cornerback Jarrian Jones.

Little suffered a knee injury and Jones hurt his chest. Neither returned to the game.

As for Tuten, he carried the ball on the Jaguars’ first play from scrimmage, and once he was tackled, he headed for the sideline. ⁠Tuten was in and out for the rest of the game as he continues to ⁠play through an ankle/foot injury that has hindered him since Nov. 1.

Herbert was 15 of 21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns ​against New York. He also ran eight times for 32 yards and another touchdown.

But the franchise quarterback took six more sacks to bring his season total to ‌39, a league high.

Herbert previously suffered an injury to the middle finger of his left (non- throwing) hand earlier this month, but it wasn’t fractured and he was able to play through it.

He was blocking for running back Christian ⁠McCaffrey and was rolled up in a pile as McCaffrey was tackled.

“That was really crushing,” Shanahan said. “Colton’s had an unbelievable year.”

Little suffered a knee injury and Jones hurt his chest. Neither returned to the game.

As for Tuten, he ‌carried the ball on the Jaguars’ first play from scrimmage, and once he was tackled, he headed for the sideline. Tuten was in and out for the rest of the game as he continues to play through an ankle/foot injury that has hindered him since Nov. 1.

Tuten led the Jaguars in rushing with 33 yards on 10 attempts. He also caught three passes for 20 yards.

Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II picked up an ankle injury on the first defensive series and was ruled out.

–Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Alex Highsmith had a great game brewing before it was spoiled by an ⁠ankle injury.

He was deemed questionable to return before being downgraded to out.

“Alex, (I) can’t say enough about him,” coach Mike McCarthy said postgame. “I mean, you just talk about his level of energy and ⁠professionalism, and so we’ll see what this brings. But yeah, I don’t ‌really have a diagnosis for you on the ankle.”

Highsmith, who had 9.5 sacks a season ago, raised his season total to 5.5 ⁠before the injury.

In the same game, the Eagles lost cornerback Quinyon Mitchell to a hamstring injury. Philadelphia held on to win 19-16.

–Both ​the Detroit Lions ‌and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers saw cornerbacks injured in their game.

Khalil Dorsey injured his wrist in the first quarter and was listed ​as questionable before ⁠returning to the game, which the Lions won 31-21 to improve to 8-2. The Buccaneers ruled out Jacob Parrish after he sustained a back injury. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) and defensive lineman Elijah Simmons (concussion) also were hurt during the contest.

–Chicago Bears running back Roschon Johnson has an ankle injury that could keep him out of the Thanksgiving Day showdown against Detroit. Johnson, who has 103 rushing yards and one touchdown on 29 carries this season, didn’t record any stats before his exit following kickoff coverage in the first quarter of Chicago’s 21-13 win over New Orleans. Saints tight end Juwan Johnson (hamstring) was injured during the game.

–Arizona Cardinals linebacker Cody Simon picked up a calf injury and did not return to the team’s 34-7 loss to Kansas City. For the Chiefs, tight end Noah Gray (rib) ​and fullback Ben VanSumeren (knee) were injured.

–San Francisco starting right tackle Colton McKivitz was carted off the field with a left leg injury in the second quarter of the 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday night ‌in Mexico ​City. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said afterward that McKivitz sustained a fractured and dislocated left ankle and will miss the ⁠rest of the season.

He was blocking for running back Christian ⁠McCaffrey and was rolled up in a pile as McCaffrey was tackled.

“That was really crushing,” Shanahan said. “Colton’s had an unbelievable year.”

McKivitz, 30, has started every regular-season and playoff game since the 2023 season. He had played in 100% of the offensive snaps (563) through nine games this season and in 17 regular-season games in 2025 (1,117 snaps).

San Francisco selected him in the fifth round of the 2020 NFL Draft out of West Virginia. He played in 28 games (five starts) his first three seasons and a total of 88 regular-season games (65 ​starts) and 10 playoff games (five starts) in his seven-year career.

Vederian Lowe replaced McKivitz at right tackle on Sunday night.

For Minnesota, starting left tackle Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) exited the game briefly during the first half and then came out in the fourth quarter.

–Ravens star running back Derrick Henry left Baltimore’s game against the Carolina Panthers in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a ⁠head injury, but he said postgame that he felt fine.

“I’m good,” he told reporters in the locker room. “Bell ⁠just rung a little bit.”

Henry finished the game with 13 carries for 94 yards and a touchdown, adding four receptions for 17 yards. The ​Ravens, though, fell 35-33 to the Panthers for their sixth straight loss.

–The Jacksonville Jaguars left their 23-18 loss to the New York Giants with injury concerns for left tackle Walker Little, running ​back Bhayshul Tuten and cornerback Jarrian Jones.

Little suffered a knee injury and Jones hurt his chest. Neither returned to the game.

As for Tuten, he ‌carried the ball on the Jaguars’ first play from scrimmage, and once he was tackled, he headed for the sideline. Tuten was in and out for the rest of the game as he continues to play through an ankle/foot injury that has hindered him since Nov. 1.

Tuten led the Jaguars in rushing with 33 yards on 10 attempts. He also caught three passes for 20 yards.

Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II picked up an ankle injury on the first defensive series and was ruled out.

–Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Alex Highsmith had a great game brewing before it was spoiled by an ⁠ankle injury.

Highsmith recorded two sacks in his first six snaps against the Eagles, including a forced fumble recovered by Philadelphia, but on the latter sack it appeared he was rolled up on.

He was deemed questionable to return before being downgraded to out.

“Alex, (I) can’t say enough about him,” coach Mike McCarthy said postgame. “I mean, you just talk about his level of energy and ⁠professionalism, and so we’ll see what this brings. But yeah, I don’t ‌really have a diagnosis for you on the ankle.”

Highsmith, who had 9.5 sacks a season ago, raised his season total to 5.5 ⁠before the injury.

In the same game, the Eagles lost cornerback Quinyon Mitchell to a hamstring injury. Philadelphia held on to win 19-16.

–Both ​the Detroit Lions ‌and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers saw cornerbacks injured in their game.

Khalil Dorsey injured his wrist in the first quarter and was listed ​as questionable before ⁠returning to the game, which the Lions won 31-21 to improve to 8-2. The Buccaneers ruled out Jacob Parrish after he sustained a back injury. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) and defensive lineman Elijah Simmons (concussion) also were hurt during the contest.

–Chicago Bears running back Roschon Johnson has an ankle injury that could keep him out of the Thanksgiving Day showdown against Detroit. Johnson, who has 103 rushing yards and one touchdown on 29 carries this season, didn’t record any stats before his exit following kickoff coverage in the first quarter of Chicago’s 21-13 win over New Orleans. Saints tight end Juwan Johnson (hamstring) was injured during the game.

–Arizona Cardinals linebacker Cody Simon picked up a calf injury and did not return to the team’s 34-7 loss to Kansas City. For the Chiefs, tight end Noah Gray (rib) ​and fullback Ben VanSumeren (knee) were injured.

(–Field Level Media)

text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are celebrating their 34-7 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, but that won’t last long. The team has to shift its focus quickly to the Buffalo Bills for a Week 12 game on Thanksgiving, with Kansas City and Buffalo meeting on “Thursday Night Football.”

Speaking to reporters after the Week 11 win over the Cardinals, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid gave his typical postgame injury update. The Chiefs suffered two injuries late in the game against Arizona.

Chiefs pick up two injuries late against the Cardinals

Chiefs FB Ben VanSumeren was ruled out with a knee injury. Meanwhile, TE Noah Gray was ruled questionable to return with a rib injury. Reid spoke briefly about both injuries after the game.

“As far as the injuries go, Noah Gray got hit in the ribs,” Reid said. “We’ll just see how he does. And then (Ben) VanSumeren tweaked his knee there. So, other than that, we came out pretty healthy.”

The problem with any injury on a short week is that players have that much less time to rest and prepare their bodies for the next game. That makes the injury status for both Gray and VanSumeren crucial to monitor when practice resumes. The Chiefs should hold at least an estimated practice on Monday, which will offer the first real look at where things stand.

Why the timing hurts Kansas City’s tight end room

These two injuries could be a massive blow to Kansas City at one specific position group. VanSumeren filled in this week as the Chiefs’ No. 4 tight end. That role opened up after TE Jared Wiley suffered a fractured ankle and landed on injured reserve this past week. After Wiley’s injury, the Chiefs signed TE John Fitzpatrick to the practice squad. They also have international player Thomas Odukoya on the practice squad at tight end.

The truth is, Kansas City simply doesn’t have much depth at tight end. Starter Travis Kelce is also playing through ankle and calf injuries. He’s a tough dude, and even Patrick Mahomes knows that it takes a lot to keep him off the football field.

“That’s Travis (Kelce),” Mahomes said. “I mean, you can’t take that dude off the football field. He loves it, and he goes out there and has success when he plays because he loves it that much. He competes. He’s gonna do whatever it takes to help the team win. And I mean, he made a couple big plays for us there, especially in the early part of the game. And that’s the type of leader he is. I’ll always say it makes my job as a quarterback easy. Like whenever you got a guy. That could take a game off, or could take practices off, or plays off, because he’s a Hall of Famer, and he’s the one that wants to get in there every single rep. That kind of gives you the mindset to tell the other guys, like, ‘Hey, like y’all want to take a rep off? Look at this guy.’ and it’s just easy for me as a leader to have someone like that on my team.”

Still, that leaves Jake Briningstool as the only fully healthy tight end on the 53-man roster. If either Gray or VanSumeren misses time, the Chiefs don’t have many options to lean on.

Chiefs have one emergency option at tight end

The good news is that Kansas City has WR Andrew Armstrong. He can line up in-line and play tight end if necessary. Armstrong also brings strength as a perimeter blocker, so the Chiefs can use him in that role if they find themselves in a pinch. However, the Chiefs will eventually have to address this injury situation at tight end. It might not happen with the short week, but they’ve got to scour their options.

Fitzpatrick hasn’t even spent a full week with the team. If Kansas City has to rely on him in any capacity against Buffalo, that would be cause for concern. NFL teams have to roll with the punches, especially on a short week. Still, the past two weeks have done a number on the Chiefs’ tight end room, and Monday’s practice estimation should reveal how much of a patchwork group Kansas City will bring to the Bills game.

text:
The 49ers are all too familiar with the kind of ankle injury Colton McKivitz suffered in their 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday at Estadio Banorte.

Coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed the injury is a broken and dislocated left ankle. Linebacker Fred Warner suffered the same injury last season, and defensive tackle Gracen Halton's rookie season was cut short by the injury just two weeks ago.

"We think it’s broken and dislocated, similar to probably Fred’s last year, so that was really crushing," Shanahan told reporters after the game. "Colton’s had an unbelievable year. We care about all our guys, but it was tough to see Colton go down like that."

The crowd noise in Mexico City fell to a hush and 49ers players were distraught as the starting right tackle was carted off in the second quarter, after his left leg was stuck under multiple players at the end of a Christian McCaffrey run. His ankle was facing the wrong direction when the pile was off of him.

McKivitz had started 100 percent of the 49ers' offensive snaps this season and entered Week 11 with the longest active consecutive streak of snaps (270) without allowing a QB hit among tackles, per PFF.

San Francisco 49ers

Find the latest San Francisco 49ers news, highlights, analysis and more with NBC Sports Bay Area and California.

But Shanahan is confident backup swing tackle Vedarian Lowe, who entered the game in McKivitz's absence, can fill the void moving forward.

"That’s why we brought Vederian here," Shanahan said. "He’s played a lot of football, and he stepped up really big in that game. He’s going to continue to do that the rest of this year for us."

The 49ers' offense continued to excel after McKivitz left the game, and San Francisco, now 9-1, will look to keep rolling as he works his way back to the field for next season.
